punchline: Graham's Mr. Market names a different price for the same share every morning. What changes is his mood, not the business.
thirty_sec: Benjamin Graham asks investors to imagine a partner in a small business, Mr. Market, who comes by each day and offers to buy your share or sell you his. On euphoric days his price is high, on gloomy days very low, while the balance sheet and earnings stay the same. You may ignore him. Check what the business is worth, and consider selling only when the price is far above it, buying only when it is far below.
